_comment: Curated metadata for the console and homebrew groups in the collection.

atari2600/Berzerk.bin.title: Berzerk
atari2600/Berzerk.bin.desc: The Atari 2600 port of Stern's maze shooter, with wandering robots, electrified walls and the relentless Evil Otto.

atari2600/Dodge Em.bin.title: Dodge 'Em
atari2600/Dodge Em.bin.desc: A top-down driving game in which the player collects dots on a roundabout while computer cars try to run them down.

atari2600/E.T. - The Extra-Terrestrial.b.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
atari2600/E.T. - The Extra-Terrestrial.b.desc: An adaptation of the film in which E.T. collects phone parts to call home, avoiding scientists and wells.
atari2600/E.T. - The Extra-Terrestrial.b.history: Designed by Howard Scott Warshaw in a famously short five-week window, E.T. is often cited in discussions of the 1983 video game crash.

atari2600/Football.bin.title: Football
atari2600/Football.bin.desc: One of the earliest console football games, using a simplified field and a single-player-versus-computer or two-player mode.

atari2600/Frogger.bin.title: Frogger
atari2600/Frogger.bin.desc: The Atari 2600 conversion of Konami's hopping arcade classic, with the highway and river crossings intact.

atari2600/Kaboom.bin.title: Kaboom!
atari2600/Kaboom.bin.desc: A paddle-controlled game in which the player catches falling bombs dropped by a robber, with speed rising every wave.

atari2600/Laser Blast.BIN.title: Laser Blast
atari2600/Laser Blast.BIN.desc: A single-screen shooter in which a flying saucer strafes ground targets while dodging enemy fire.

atari2600/Maze Craze.BIN.title: Maze Craze
atari2600/Maze Craze.BIN.desc: A top-down maze chase with dozens of selectable maze and visibility options, including invisible walls.

atari2600/Night Drive.BIN.title: Night Driver
atari2600/Night Drive.BIN.desc: A first-person night-time driving game built from simple white roadside markers against a black screen.

atari2600/Pitfall.bin.title: Pitfall!
atari2600/Pitfall.bin.desc: Pitfall Harry runs, swings and jumps through a jungle of crocodiles, quicksand and scorpions to collect treasure.
atari2600/Pitfall.bin.history: Designed by David Crane, Pitfall! was one of the first console games built around a large, scrolling world.

atari2600/Space Invaders.bin.title: Space Invaders
atari2600/Space Invaders.bin.desc: The Atari 2600 version of Taito's arcade landmark, adapted for the console's joystick and limited hardware.

atari2600/Yar (Revision).bin.title: Yars' Revenge
atari2600/Yar (Revision).bin.desc: A shield-busting shooter in which a Yar attacks the Qotile with a Zorlon Cannon while dodging a swirling destroyer missile.
atari2600/Yar (Revision).bin.history: Designed by Howard Scott Warshaw, Yars' Revenge is widely regarded as one of the Atari 2600's best original games.

gba/Fire Emblem - Sealed Sword.gba.title: Fire Emblem: Fūin no Tsurugi (Sealed Sword)
gba/Fire Emblem - Sealed Sword.gba.desc: A Japan-only Game Boy Advance tactical RPG following Roy across the continent of Elibe, with permanent unit death and weapon-triangle combat.
gba/Fire Emblem - Sealed Sword.gba.history: Released only in Japan, Fūin no Tsurugi is the sixth Fire Emblem and the game that introduced Roy, later popularised through Super Smash Bros. Melee.
gba/Fire Emblem - Sealed Sword.gba.notes: The collection's filename is 'Fire Emblem - Sealed Sword', which corresponds to the Japanese title Fūin no Tsurugi (The Binding Blade). It is not The Sacred Stones, whose Japanese title is Seima no Kōseki.

gba/Mother 3.gba.title: Mother 3
gba/Mother 3.gba.desc: A Japan-only RPG about a family on the Nowhere Islands, combining a rhythm-based battle system with a bittersweet story.
gba/Mother 3.gba.history: Long delayed and released only in Japan on the GBA, Mother 3 has since received a well-known fan translation.

gba/Pokemon Emerald.gba.title: Pokémon Emerald
gba/Pokemon Emerald.gba.desc: The definitive third version of the Hoenn-generation Pokémon games, adding the Battle Frontier and an expanded story.

gba/Pokemon FireRed.gba.title: Pokémon FireRed
gba/Pokemon FireRed.gba.desc: A remake of the original Pokémon Red for the Game Boy Advance, set in Kanto with the Sevii Islands added.

gba/Pokemon Leafgreen.gba.title: Pokémon LeafGreen
gba/Pokemon Leafgreen.gba.desc: The companion version to FireRed, sharing its Kanto setting and adding version-exclusive Pokémon.

gba/Pokemon Ruby.gba.title: Pokémon Ruby
gba/Pokemon Ruby.gba.desc: The first Hoenn-generation Pokémon game, introducing double battles, abilities and 135 new creatures.

gba/PowerPig.gba.title: PowerPig
gba/PowerPig.gba.desc: A Game Boy Advance title held in the collection under the filename PowerPig.gba. Its release details have not been verified.

nds/0201 - Mario Kart DS (E)(Spliff).nds.title: Mario Kart DS
nds/0201 - Mario Kart DS (E)(Spliff).nds.desc: The first handheld Mario Kart with online play, introducing mission mode, retro cups and the snaking drift technique.
nds/0201 - Mario Kart DS (E)(Spliff).nds.notes: The inventory filename carries a '(Spliff)' group tag, which typically indicates a ROM release-group tag rather than game content. The matching .dsv file in the inventory is a save file and is not a game.

n64/Mario Kart 64 (USA).n64.title: Mario Kart 64
n64/Mario Kart 64 (USA).n64.desc: The Nintendo 64 sequel to Super Mario Kart, moving the series into 3D with four-player split-screen racing.

n64/Super Mario 64 (USA).n64.title: Super Mario 64
n64/Super Mario 64 (USA).n64.desc: The launch title that defined 3D platforming, with 120 Power Stars spread across Peach's castle and its painted worlds.

n64/The Legend of Zelda Majora's Mask.n6.title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
n64/The Legend of Zelda Majora's Mask.n6.desc: A darker Zelda built around a three-day time loop, mask transformations and the looming fall of the moon on Termina.

n64/Super Smash Bros.title: Super Smash Bros.
n64/Super Smash Bros.desc: A crossover fighting game in which Nintendo characters battle on themed stages, with damage percentage replacing health bars.
n64/Super Smash Bros.notes: The inventory lists this title as a folder; the files inside it are not itemised in the source listing.

love/mari0.love.title: Mari0
love/mari0.love.desc: A free fan-made mash-up that combines Super Mario Bros. level design with Portal's portal gun, distributed as a LÖVE game package.
love/mari0.love.notes: Distributed as a .love package, which is a zip archive run by the LÖVE framework rather than a console ROM.
